references.text: Moses responds to God's promise of His presence by saying that if God's face does not go with them, they should not leave from there.
The promise of rest (הֲנִחֹתִי) points forward to the rest God will give Israel in the promised land.
Isaiah refers to God's angel of His presence who saved Israel, and that God carried them and led them all the days of old.
God's rest is mentioned in connection with Israel's journey through the wilderness, where God swore that they would not enter into His rest.
The fulfillment of God's promise of rest when the Lord gave Israel peace from all their enemies around them.
God promises to teach and show the way, and to keep watch over the one who walks – parallel to God's present guidance.
The Letter to the Hebrews connects God's rest to the future Sabbath rest that remains for God's people, with reference to the wilderness journey.
Jesus promises rest (ἀνάπαυσιν) to all who come to Him and take up His yoke – a fulfillment of God's promise of rest.
Both verses connect God's presence directly to a gift of rest/peace as a result of His covenant.
